title: Beyond the Postcard: What Really Happens When You Travel Abroad
title_zh: 明信片之外：出国旅行究竟改变了你什么
intro_zh: 本文约 960 词，围绕旅行如何开阔眼界展开，含 6 个 CET-4 核心词（adapt、unfamiliar、tolerate、curiosity、perspective、confidence），建议阅读时间 10 分钟。

paragraphs.en: Maria, a twenty-year-old student from Chengdu, had planned her first trip to Italy for months. She had read the guidebooks, saved maps on her phone, and practiced how to say thank you in Italian. Yet nothing in those books prepared her for the morning she stood in a small bakery in Bologna, pointing at a flat bread she could not name. The woman behind the counter laughed, cut a warm piece, and held it out. 'Try it,' she said in slow English. 'Then you will know.' Maria later told her friends that those five minutes taught her more than a whole term of lectures.
paragraphs.zh: 来自成都的二十岁学生玛丽亚为她的第一次意大利之行准备了几个月。她读了旅行指南，把地图存在手机里，还练习了如何用意大利语说谢谢。然而那些书里没有任何内容能让她准备好面对那个早晨：她站在博洛尼亚一家小面包店里，指着一个她叫不出名字的扁平面饼。柜台后的女人笑了，切下一块温热的饼递过来。“尝尝看，”她用慢速英语说，“然后你就知道了。”玛丽亚后来告诉朋友，那五分钟教给她的东西比整整一学期的课还多。

paragraphs.en: Most of us have heard that travel broadens the mind. The interesting question is why. Researchers who study creativity have found that it is not the number of kilometers you fly that matters, but how deeply you engage with a place. In a well-known study, people who had lived abroad were more likely to come up with creative solutions than people who had never left home. The key, the researchers explained, was the willingness to adapt: those who had to adjust to a new language, new food and new rules of politeness gained something that tourists staying inside a hotel rarely do.
paragraphs.zh: 我们大多数人都听过“旅行开阔眼界”这句话。有趣的问题是：为什么？研究创造力的学者发现，重要的不是你飞了多少公里，而是你对一个地方的投入有多深。在一项著名研究中，曾在国外生活过的人比从未离开过家乡的人更容易提出有创意的解决方案。研究者解释说，关键在于是否愿意去 adapt：那些不得不去适应新语言、新食物和新礼貌规则的人，得到了住在酒店里的游客很少得到的东西。

paragraphs.en: Your brain is built to notice what is new. When you walk through a street where the signs, smells and sounds are all unfamiliar, the brain works harder: it compares, guesses and stores. Scientists call this novelty, and it activates the same reward system that makes us enjoy music or games. This extra effort is tiring — many travelers feel exhausted after a day of doing very little — but it is exactly the kind of exercise that keeps thinking flexible. A familiar street asks nothing of you; an unfamiliar one asks questions all day long.
paragraphs.zh: 你的大脑天生就会注意新事物。当你走在一条路牌、气味和声音都 unfamiliar 的街道上，大脑会更加卖力地工作：比较、猜测、储存。科学家把这种现象称为“新奇性”，它会激活与听音乐、玩游戏时相同的奖赏系统。这种额外的努力很累人——许多旅行者几乎没做什么事却觉得精疲力尽——但正是这类“锻炼”让思维保持灵活。熟悉的街道对你毫无要求；陌生的街道则一整天都在向你提问。

paragraphs.en: Travel also teaches people to tolerate not knowing. In a foreign train station, you may buy the wrong ticket, miss a stop, or sit in silence because you cannot follow a fast conversation. None of that is comfortable, yet it is rarely dangerous. Over time, travelers learn to live with small uncertainties instead of panicking. Teachers and employers often say this skill matters more than perfect grammar: the ability to stay calm, ask again, and try another way when the first plan fails.
paragraphs.zh: 旅行还教会人们 tolerate“不知道”的状态。在国外的火车站，你可能会买错票、坐过站，或者因为听不懂语速很快的对话而沉默地坐着。这些都不舒服，但很少真的危险。随着时间推移，旅行者学会与小小的不确定共处，而不是惊慌失措。老师和雇主常说，这种能力比完美的语法更重要：在第一个计划失败时保持冷静、再问一次、换一种办法。

paragraphs.en: Another change is quieter: travel feeds curiosity. At home, most of us stop asking why. We take the bus, buy the milk, and never wonder how anything works. Abroad, everything becomes a question. Why do the shops close for three hours in the afternoon? Why does this family eat from one large plate? Why do people take off their shoes at the door? Asking those questions, and listening to the answers, is a habit that many travelers carry home with them.
paragraphs.zh: 另一种变化更安静：旅行会滋养 curiosity。在家里，我们大多数人不再问“为什么”。我们坐公交、买牛奶，从不去想这些东西是怎么运作的。而在国外，一切都成了问题。为什么商店下午要关三个小时？为什么这家人从一个大盘子里一起吃饭？为什么人们进门要脱鞋？提出这些问题，并认真听答案，是许多旅行者会带回家的习惯。

paragraphs.en: The biggest gift may be a new perspective on your own life. Standing outside your own culture, you begin to see which habits are choices rather than natural laws. A student from Shanghai who spent a summer in a small German town noticed that her neighbors had dinner at six and spent the evening walking, not working. She did not decide to copy them, but she went home asking a new question: which parts of my busy routine do I actually want? Seeing your own country from a distance is like looking at your handwriting after years of not noticing it.
paragraphs.zh: 最大的礼物或许是对自己生活的一种新 perspective。站在自己的文化之外，你会开始看清哪些习惯只是选择，而不是自然法则。一位在上海读书、在德国小镇度过一个夏天的学生注意到，她的邻居六点吃晚饭，然后整个晚上都在散步，而不是工作。她并没有决定照搬，但回家时她开始问一个新问题：我忙碌的日程里，哪些部分其实是我真正想要的？从远处看自己的国家，就像多年之后重新端详自己的字迹。

paragraphs.en: This shift often shows up as confidence. Booking a hostel, asking a stranger for directions, and eating a dish you cannot identify are small victories, but they add up. A 2019 survey of young travelers found that most reported feeling more independent after a trip of two weeks or more, even when things went wrong. Interestingly, the difficult moments — the lost wallet, the wrong bus — were the ones people remembered as proof that they could manage.
paragraphs.zh: 这种转变常常表现为 confidence。订一家青年旅舍、向陌生人问路、吃一道自己认不出的菜，都是小小的胜利，但它们会累积起来。一项 2019 年针对年轻旅行者的调查发现，大多数人在两周以上的旅行后表示自己更独立了，即使途中出过差错。有趣的是，那些艰难时刻——丢了钱包、坐错车——恰恰是人们记在心里、用来证明“我能应付”的经历。

paragraphs.en: Yet travel does not automatically widen the mind. A tour bus that carries you from photo spot to photo spot can leave you with a full camera and an unchanged mind. Resorts and shopping streets look similar in Bangkok, Dubai and Paris. Even independent travelers can spend a whole trip inside a digital bubble, chatting with friends at home and watching videos in their own language. The difference lies in contact: talking to local people, trying food you cannot pronounce, and letting a place interrupt your plans.
paragraphs.zh: 不过，旅行并不会自动让人开阔眼界。一辆把你从一个拍照点送到另一个拍照点的观光巴士，可能只留给你满满一相机的照片和一颗没变的心。在曼谷、迪拜和巴黎，度假村和购物街看起来都很相似。即使是自由行的旅行者，也可能整趟旅程都待在一个“数字气泡”里，和家里的朋友聊天、看母语的视频。差别在于接触：和当地人交谈、尝试叫不出名字的食物、允许一个地方打乱你的计划。

paragraphs.en: So how should you travel if you want the effect? Go slowly. Stay in one city long enough to find your favorite bakery. Learn twenty words of the local language and use them badly. Take the local bus, eat where the queue is full of residents, and travel alone at least once. Keep a small notebook and write down one surprise each day. The passport stamp fades, and the photographs stay in your phone, but the wider way of thinking stays with you.
paragraphs.zh: 那么，如果你想要这种效果，应该怎么旅行？慢一点。在一座城市待得足够久，久到能找到你最喜欢的那家面包店。学二十个当地语言的词，然后磕磕绊绊地用出来。坐当地的公交车，去排队的都是本地人的地方吃饭，并且至少独自旅行一次。带一个小本子，每天记下一个让你意外的事。护照上的印章会褪色，照片会留在手机里，但那种更开阔的思维方式会一直跟着你。

questions.q: According to the passage, what did the study of people who had lived abroad suggest?
options: The number of kilometers flown is the main factor in creative thinking.
Being willing to adapt to a new culture matters more than simply being far from home.
Living abroad always makes people more intelligent than others.
Only people who speak two languages can benefit from travel.
questions.explain: 第二段明确指出，研究的关键不是飞行距离，而是“the willingness to adapt”，即愿意适应新语言、新食物和新礼貌规则的人收获更多。选项 0 与原文相反，选项 2、3 属于绝对化或原文未提及的推断。

questions.q: What does the author mean by 'a digital bubble'?
options: A hotel room that offers very fast internet.
A travel app that plans every step of a trip.
Staying connected to home online instead of joining local life.
A camera that is full of photographs.
questions.explain: 第八段说，即使是自由行的旅行者也可能整趟旅程都在“数字气泡”里——和家里的朋友聊天、看母语视频；结合上下文可知它指“身在外地却仍沉浸在手机与家乡的网络世界里，不接触当地生活”。

questions.q: Why does the author mention the student from Shanghai who spent a summer in a small German town?
options: To prove that German towns are much quieter than Chinese cities.
To show that travel can make people question their own daily habits.
To argue that working in the evening is a harmful habit.
To explain why Europeans usually eat dinner early.
questions.explain: 第六段用这位学生的例子说明，站在自己文化之外能让人看清哪些习惯只是“选择”，并促使她回家后重新审视自己忙碌的日程，这正是旅行带来新视角的体现。

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To persuade readers to give up tour buses completely.
To explain how travel can widen the mind and how to make it happen.
To compare the food of Italy, Morocco and Germany.
To list the dangers of traveling alone in foreign countries.
questions.explain: 全文先说明旅行开阔眼界的机制（适应、新奇、容忍不确定、好奇、视角、自信），最后指出并非所有旅行都有效并给出具体建议，因此主旨是“解释旅行如何开阔思维以及如何做到”。其他选项都只是文中的细节或文中并未主张的观点。
